title: Class-Classification Dependency Envy (Rental vs. Movie)
pattern: A struct method branches (`match` or `if let`) on an enumeration or type-code of an associated object to calculate values, rather than delegating the type-based calculation to the type itself.
why_bad: If a new movie classification (e.g., "Sci-Fi") is added, the `Rental` struct must be modified. Type-specific variations should be encapsulated inside the class representing that type (or via polymorphism/traits).
detection: A method matching on `self.associated_field.classification` and performing different arithmetic paths.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If the calculation depends heavily on the `Rental`'s properties (`days_rented`) and changing the movie structure to know about days rented would introduce a cyclic dependency.
